units: pixels (x right, y down, full-resolution 1920x1080) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the sea-floor strip vs the median background: |shift| <= 0.1 px (half-res) in every 4th frame; the background is identical apart from animated caustics on the sand and faint light rays
camera.view: side view, camera horizontal; the shark swims parallel to the image plane (2D scene). Shark apparent height constant (bbox 161/162 -> 431-433 px all clip); full silhouette length 926-928 px at frames 15-20 and 914-919 px at frames 24-30 (body flex / slight yaw, <=1.5 %)

objects.name: shark
objects.description: single grey-blue shark (great-white-like: pale snout and belly, gill slits, tall dorsal fin, crescent tail). The only moving object.
objects.visible_frames: 0-46 (frame 47: gone). Fully inside the image in frames 15-30. The snout enters first: the rear body/tail is cut by the right edge in frames 0-14; the snout is cut by the left edge from frame 31 on.
objects.direction: right to left (-x), horizontal; no vertical motion (top/bottom of mask constant within +-1 px)
objects.reference_point: origin_x_est / origin_y_est = estimated centre of the full silhouette bbox (proxy for the rig origin). Frames 6-38 from the dorsal-fin apex (+15.4 px), 0-5 from the snout tip (+459.6), 39-46 from the tail tip (-453.2). origin_y = 297 px constant.

size_px_full_view.body_depth_px_approx_note: trunk depth without fins is about 140-150 px near the gills (visual estimate from overlay)

motion_summary_px.note: per-frame steps of the dorsal apex 56-61 px (feature noise +-1.5 px); snout steps start at 37 (0->1), 51, 55, 52, 56 for frames 1-5; tail-tip steps ~56 at frames 39-46. Different body points give slightly different speeds because the body flexes (see notes.md).

static_objects.name: sea_floor

static_objects.image_region: y from ~795-1030 (top edge varies with x: e.g. x=0 ->832, x=600 ->989, x=1080 ->795, x=1440 ->1031) to 1080, full width
